context_requirements: Mucolytic agents act on extracellular mucus components (e.g., disulfide bonds in mucin glycoproteins) and do not require intracellular targets.

A transcriptional response would require the cell line to express and secrete mucins or mucus-associated proteins; the nine tested lines are non-airway/non-glandular and are not expected to produce a mucus layer.
No annotated molecular target is listed for this class, so no direct transcriptional program is expected.
falsifiers: Reproducible concentration-dependent changes in the 978 landmark genes at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine cell lines.
Shared transcriptional signature across multiple lines that is not explained by vehicle or general stress.
Evidence of direct modulation of a known mucolytic target (e.g., disulfide bond reduction) leading to downstream gene expression changes in these cells.
